concepts.title: Cylinder volume
concepts.explanation: A cylinder has volume πr²h, equal to circular base area times perpendicular height. Volume is measured in cubic units.

example.problem: A cylinder has diameter 4 cm and height 6 cm. Find its volume in cm³.

concepts.commonMistake: Use radius, not diameter, in r².

concepts.title: Cone volume and recasting
concepts.explanation: A cone has volume πr²h/3. Its perpendicular height differs from its slant height. When material is recast without loss, total volume stays constant.

example.problem: A cone of radius 3 cm has volume 18π cm³. Find its perpendicular height in cm.

concepts.commonMistake: Omitting the factor 1/3 makes the cone volume three times too large.
checklist: Equate volumes when material is conserved.

concepts.title: Hemisphere surface area
concepts.explanation: A hemisphere has curved area 2πr² and total area 3πr² when its circular base is included. State which surfaces are exposed.

example.problem: Find the total surface area in cm² of a hemisphere of radius 2 cm, including its base.

concepts.commonMistake: Curved area excludes the flat circular base.
checklist: Use curved or total area accordingly.

concepts.title: Combined solids and volume conservation
concepts.explanation: Add non-overlapping component volumes to find a composite solid’s volume. For recasting, divide total material volume by the volume of one new piece.

example.problem: A solid cylinder of radius 3 cm and height 2 cm is topped by a hemisphere of radius 3 cm. Find total volume in cm³.

concepts.commonMistake: Do not add surface areas when the question asks for volume.
checklist: Use equal volumes if material is recast.

concepts.title: Exposed surface area
concepts.explanation: Trace the surfaces visible outside a combined solid. Joined faces are internal and must be excluded; an exposed base must be included if requested.

example.problem: A cone has radius 6 cm and perpendicular height 8 cm. Find total surface area in cm² including its base.

concepts.commonMistake: Adding total areas of components double-counts their joined faces.
